==============================================================================\n384\t\n385\t/**\n386\t * Check if a receiver state can be resumed (D22).\n387\t *\n388\t * Resume is NOT supported when     docs/notes/bf-2vke-compression-resume-t4-reap-interaction.md\n400\t */\n401\texport function canResumeRecv(state: RecvSessionState): boolean {\n402\t  if (state.type !== 'paused' && state.type !== * Check if bitmap is complete (all bits set).\n432\t */\n433\texport function isBitmapComplete(bitmap: Uint8Array): boolean {\n434\t  for (const byte of bitmap) {\n435\t    if (byte !== 0xff) {\n436\t      return false;\n437\t    }\n438\t  }\n439\t  return true;\n440\t}\n441\t\n442\t/**\n443\t * Clear a bit in the bitmap (for E12 block hash failure).\n444\t */\n445\texport function bitIndex);\n449\t}\n450\t\n451\t/**\n452\t * Set a bit in the bitmap (block complete).\n453\t */\n454\texport function setBitmapBit(bitmap: Uint8Array, blockIndex: number): void {\n455\t  const ==============================================================================\n461\t// BLOCK POSITION TRACKING FOR WRITES\n462\t// ==============================================================================\n463\t\n464\t/**\n465\t * Concrete implementation of WritePositionTracker.\n466\t *\n467\t * Manages block position tracking for out-of-order writes.\n468\t * Integrates with the bitmap-based tracking in BaseRecvState.\n469\t */\n470\texport class WritePositionTrackerImpl implements WritePositionTracker {\n471\t  private _currentPosition: number;\n472\t  private _blocksWritten: number;\n473\t  private readonly state: BaseRecvState;\n474\t\n475\t  constructor(state: BaseRecvState) {\n476\t    this.state = state;\n477\t    this._currentPosition = 0;\n478\t    this._blocksWritten = 0;\n479\t\n480\t    // Initialize from existing state\n481\t    this._blocksWritten = getBlocksWrittenCount(state);\n482\t    this._currentPosition = getCurrentWritePosition(state);\n483\t  }\n484\t\n485\t  /**\n486\t   * Current write position as block index.\n487\t   * Tracks the next expected block to be written.\n488\t   */\n489\t  get currentPosition(): number {\n490\t    return this._currentPosition;\n491\t  }\n492\t\n493\t  /**\n494\t   * Total number of blocks written so far.\n495\t   */\n496\t  get the current position.\n503\t   */\n504\t  getNextPosition(): number {\n505\t    return getNextWritePosition(this.state, this._currentPosition);\n506\t  }\n507\t\n508\t  /**\n509\t   * Update position after a successful write.\n510\t   * Advances to the next incomplete block.\n511\t   */\n512\t  advancePosition(): void {\n513\t    // Find next unwritten block\n514\t    const nextPos = this.getNextPosition();\n515\t\n516\t    // If we found a new unwritten block, advance to it\n517\t    if (nextPos !== this._currentPosition) {\n518\t      this._currentPosition = nextPos;\n519\t    } written count\n525\t    this._blocksWritten = getBlocksWrittenCount(this.state);\n526\t  }\n527\t\n528\t  /**\n529\t   * Reset position to a specific block index.\n530\t   * Used during resume or ${position} (must be 0-${this.state.meta.blockCount})`);\n535\t    }\n536\t    this._currentPosition = position;\n537\t  }\n538\t\n539\t  /**\n540\t   * Mark a block as written and update position blockIndex)) {\n545\t      markBlockWritten(this.state, blockIndex);\n546\t      this._blocksWritten++;\n547\t\n548\t      // If this was the current position, advance to next\n549\t      if (blockIndex === this._currentPosition) {\n550\t        this.advancePosition();\n551\t      }\n552\t    }\n553\t  }\n554\t\n555\t  /**\n556\t   * Check if a block has been written.\n557\t   */\n558\t  isBlockWritten(blockIndex: number): boolean {\n559\t    return isBlockWritten(this.state, blockIndex);\n560\t  }\n561\t\n562\t  /**\n563\t   * Get all unwritten block indices.\n564\t   */\n565\t return getWriteProgress(this.state);\n581\t  }\n582\t}\n583\t\n584\t/**\n585\t * Check if a block has been written to output.\n586\t */\n587\texport function isBlockWritten(state: BaseRecvState, blockIndex: number): boolean {\n588\t  const byteIndex = Math.floor(blockIndex / 8);\n589\t  const bitIndex = blockIndex % 8;\n590\t  return (state.writtenBlocks[byteIndex] & (1 << bitIndex)) !== 0;\n591\t}\n592\t\n593\t/**\n594\t * Mark a block as written to output.\n595\t */\n596\texport function markBlockWritten(state: BaseRecvState, blockIndex: number): void {\n597\t  const byteIndex = far.\n604\t */\n605\texport function getBlocksWrittenCount(state: BaseRecvState): number {\n606\t  let count = 0;\n607\t  for (const byte of state.writtenBlocks) {\n608\t    count +=     unwritten.push(i);\n639\t    }\n640\t  }\n641\t\n642\t  return unwritten;\n643\t}\n644\t\n645\t/**\n646\t * Check if all complete blocks have been written.\n647\t */\n648\texport function 8);\n653\t    const bitIndex = i % 8;\n654\t\n655\t    const complete = (state.complete[byteIndex] & (1 << bitIndex)) !== 0;\n656\t    const written = (state.writtenBlocks[byteIndex] & (1 << }\n677\t  }\n678\t\n679\t  return blockCount; // All blocks written\n680\t}\n681\t\n682\t/**\n683\t * Get the current write position as a block index.\n684\t * Returns the index of the next block to blockIndex: number,\n711\t  blockSize: number\n712\t): Promise<void> {\n713\t  // Check if block is already written\n714\t  if (isBlockWritten(state, blockIndex)) {\n715\t    throw new Error(`Block progress ratio (0.0 = none written, 1.0 = all written)\n750\t */\n751\texport function getWriteProgress(state: BaseRecvState): number {\n752\t  const total = state.meta.blockCount;\n753\t  if (total === 0) return 1.0;\n754\t  const written = getBlocksWrittenCount(state);\n755\t  return written / total;\n756\t}\n757\t\n758\t// ==============================================================================\n759\t// RESUME TOKEN (D22)\n760\t// ==============================================================================\n761\t\n762\t/**\n763\t * Resume token for persisting session state.\n764\t */\n765\texport interface ResumeToken {\n766\t  streamId: number;\n767\t  meta: BeaconMeta;\n768\t  complete: Uint8Array;  // bitmap of complete blocks\n769\t  writtenBlocks: Uint8Array;  // bitmap of written blocks\n770\t  timestamp: number;\n771\t}\n772\t\n773\t/**\n774\t * Create a resume token from a resumable state.\n775\t *\n776\t * When compression is enabled, resume is NOT supported because:\n777\t * - CompressionStream offers no determinism guarantee across browser restarts\n778\t * - Re-compression after staging reaping (E11) may produce different bytes\n779\t * - Different bytes → different block boundaries → different hashes\n780\t * - Receiver's persisted bitmap would become silently invalid\n781\t *\n782\t * **This implements Option B from bf-3k90:** \"Forbid resume when compression is enabled\"\n783\t Resume/Compression/T4-Reap Conflict Analysis\n\n## Problem Statement\n\n**plan.md §8.3 claims**: \"the sender is stateless across restarts by construction\" — **FALSE when compression is enabled**.\n\n### Root Cause Chain\n\n1. **Wire payload depends on compressed staging file** (D8): CompressionStream writes a compressed staging file to OPFS, then blocks are carved from it\n2. **CompressionStream offers no determinism guarantee**: Different runs, versions, or platforms may produce different compressed byte sequences for the same input\n3. **E11 reaps staging on startup**: Sender-side staging files with no active session are deleted on startup\n4. **T4 requires wiping staging for privacy**: Staging MUST be wiped on completion, cancel, and startup-reap\n5. **Sender restart → staging reaped → re-compress**: When the sender restarts, it re-compresses the source file\n6. **Different bytes → different blocks**: Re-compression produces different byte boundaries\n7. **Receiver silently corrupted**: The receiver's bitmap, block hashes, and manifest assume the old block boundaries — everything becomes invalid without detection\n\n### Why This Breaks Resume\n\n**When compression is DISABLED** (the original design):\n- Sender is stateless: Same file + same streamId = same blocks\n- streamId derived deterministically from file metadata (§7.4)\n- Receiver's bitmap stays valid across sender restarts\n\n**When compression is ENABLED**:\n- Sender's wire payload = compressed staging file\n- CompressionStream non-deterministic → re-compression produces different bytes\n- Same streamId, different block contents → receiver's bitmap points to wrong data\n- Per-block hashes (the only application-layer integrity check, §7.1) fail silently until final verification\n- Multi-GB transfer completes with corrupt output\n\n## Resolution: Forbid Resume with Compression\n\n**Decision**: Resume is NOT supported when compression is enabled.\n\n### Implementation\n\n1. **Beacon flag `RESUME_DISABLED`** (PacketFlags or beacon flags field)\n   - Sender sets this flag when `PacketFlags.Compressed` is set\n   - Receiver reads this flag from the beacon\n   - Resume UI is suppressed when this flag is present\n\n2. **Privacy constraint preserved** (T4):\n   - Staging files continue to be wiped on startup (E11)\n   - Staging files continue to be wiped on completion/cancel\n   - No change to privacy posture\n\n3. **User experience**:\n   - User selects same file → different streamId than compressed session → fresh transfer\n   - Receiver never offers resume for compressed transfers\n   - No silent corruption possible\n\n### Why This Over Alternatives\n\n**Alternative 1**: Preserve staging across restarts\n- **Rejected**: Violates T4 (privacy requirement)\n- Would require user-visible \"abandoned staging files\" clutter\n- Storage quota pressure on multi-GB files\n\n**Alternative 2**: Hash-based block boundaries\n- **Rejected**: Requires full file read to compute block boundaries\n- Defeats streaming design (D20)\n- Adds complexity for minimal benefit\n\n**Alternative 3**: Compression determinism guarantee\n- **Rejected**: CompressionStream spec offers no such guarantee\n- Would require custom WASM compressor\n- Out of scope for v1\n\n**Alternative 4**: Per-block hash mismatch detection during resume\n- **Rejected**: Requires receiver to re-verify all completed blocks on resume\n- Wastes progress (hours of transfer time)\n- Poor UX: \"resume works but throws away your work\"\n\n## Specification\n\n### Sender Behavior\n\nWhen compression is enabled:\n1. Set `PacketFlags.Compressed` on beacon packets\n2. Set `RESUME_DISABLED` flag in beacon metadata\n3. Continue normal transmission\n4. Wipe staging on completion/cancel (T4)\n5. Staging reaped on next startup (E11)\n\n### Receiver Behavior\n\nOn beacon receipt:\n1. If `RESUME_DISABLED` flag is set:\n   - Do NOT persist resume state (bitmap, metadata)\n   - Show \"Resume not available for this transfer\" message\n   - Suppress any resume UI on reload\n2. Otherwise, persist resume state normally (D22)\n\n### streamId Behavior\n\nstreamId derivation (§7.4) is UNCHANGED:\n- Same file → same streamId regardless of compression\n- This is intentional: user re-selecting file starts fresh transfer\n- Different compressed session cannot resume from/to uncompressed session\n\n## Testing\n\n### Unit Tests\n- Test that beacon sets `RESUME_DISABLED` when compression enabled\n- Test that receiver suppresses resume UI when flag present\n\n### Integration Tests\n- Compressed transfer interrupted → reload → resume UI NOT shown\n- Uncompressed transfer interrupted → reload → resume UI shown\n- Compressed then uncompressed transfer → different streamIds\n\n### Property Tests\n- For any file, compression produces deterministic blocks within ONE session\n- For any file, re-compression MAY produce different blocks across sessions\n\n## References\n\n- plan.md §8.3 (Resume D22)\n- plan.md §7.4 (streamId derivation)\n- plan.md §7.1 (Packet header and integrity)\n- plan.md §12 (Threat model T4)\n- plan.md §10 (Edge cases E11, E12)\n- plan.md D8 (Compression decision)\n- plan.md D22 (Resume requirement)\n","numLines":125,"startLine":1,"totalLines":125}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_54f4087808984985975f5eb9","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# screenferry\n2\t\n3\t**Move a file between two devices using nothing but a screen and a camera.**\n4\t\n5\tscreenferry is a static web app — no server, no backend, no network between the two\n6\tdevices. The sending device reads a local file and flashes it out as an animated\n7\tsequence of optical codes. The receiving device runs the *same* web app, points\n8\tits camera at the sender's screen, decodes the frames, and reassembles the\n9\toriginal file byte-for-byte.\n10\t\n11\t```\n12\t┌─────────────────┐                      ┌─────────────────┐\n13\t│    SENDER       │   ░▓█ optical ░▓█    │    RECEIVER     │\n14\t│                 │  ──────────────────► │                 │\n15\t│  file → chunks  │  animated code frames│  frames → file  │\n16\t│  → coded frames │   screen to camera   │  → download     │\n17\t└─────────────────┘                      └─────────────────┘\n18\t        same static web app on both ends\n19\t```\n20\t\n21\tAnimated QR codes are the obvious way to do this, and the likely starting point —\n22\tbut the goal is the *channel*, not the format. QR spends most of its capacity on\n23\trobustness screenferry doesn't need (arbitrary angles, print damage, one bit per\n24\tmodule). Denser modulation — colored cells, stacked RGB codes, a purpose-built\n25\tgrid codec — is on the table wherever it survives a real phone camera. The\n26\tarchitecture keeps that layer swappable.\n27\t\n28\t## Why\n29\t\n30\tThe screen-to-camera channel is the one data path that survives when everything\n31\telse is unavailable or untrusted:\n32\t\n33\t- **Air-gapped systems** — the receiving machine is deliberately not on any network.\n34\t- **Hostile or captive networks** — hotel wifi, conference NAT, corporate DLP.\n35\t- **Cross-ecosystem transfer** — AirDrop doesn't talk to Android; Nearby Share doesn't talk to iOS.\n36\t- **No pairing, no accounts, no cloud** — nothing is uploaded anywhere, because\n37\t  there is nowhere to upload it to. The bytes go from screen to lens.\n38\t- **Provably no exfiltration** — a static page with no network calls can be\n39\t  audited once and trusted thereafter.\n40\t\n41\t## The hard part\n42\t\n43\tThe channel is **strictly one-way**. The sender has no idea how the receiver is\n44\tdoing — there is no ACK, no retransmit request, no back-channel of any kind. The\n45\treceiver *will* miss frames: autofocus hunting, motion blur, glare, the user\n46\tlooking away.\n47\t\n48\tA naive \"loop through chunks 1..N forever\" transfer degrades badly under loss\n49\t(the coupon-collector problem — the last few chunks take agonizingly long).\n50\tscreenferry's design centers on **rateless erasure coding**: the sender emits an\n51\tendless stream of encoded frames, and the receiver reconstructs the file once it\n52\thas collected *any* sufficient subset. Miss a frame and it simply doesn't\n53\tmatter — the next one is just as useful.\n54\t\n55\t## Status\n56\t\n57\t**Research complete. Phase 1 core codec built (22 tests green). Phase 0 harness and Phase 0.5 spike both partial** — see [`docs/plan/plan.md`](docs/plan/plan.md) §17.2.\n58\t\n59\t- [`docs/plan/plan.md`](docs/plan/plan.md) — the complete application plan\n60\t- [`docs/notes/`](docs/notes/) — design decisions and constraints specific to screenferry\n61\t- [`docs/research/`](docs/research/) — findings:\n62\t  - `qr-encoding-capacity.md` — QR versions, EC levels, bytes per frame, JS encoders\n63\t  - `browser-qr-scanning.md` — camera capture, decoder libraries, binary safety\n64\t  - `fountain-codes-and-protocol.md` — erasure coding for a one-way channel, wire format\n65\t  - `beyond-qr-optical-channels.md` — color barcodes, screen-camera research, what beats QR\n66\t  - `custom-codec-engineering.md` — feasibility of a purpose-built codec in a browser\n67\t  - `pwa-platform-and-ux.md` — offline PWA, file I/O, iOS constraints, UX, testing\n68\t\n69\t## Expectations\n70\t\n71\tThis is not a fast pipe. Realistic throughput is on the order of **kilobytes per\n72\tsecond** — good for keys, configs, documents, and small archives; not for video.\n73\tThe app is designed to be honest about this up front rather than let a user start\n74\ta transfer that would take an hour.\n75\t\n76\t## License\n77\t\n78\tMIT\n79\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":"call_ab7afd1283974e1c9e847367","session_id":"c99a1aaf-2bac-4a1c-9621-cc373f75e651","uuid":"b708a719-e9a1-4fb4-8d00-997cfe32e784","timestamp":"2026-08-02T16:06:00.869Z","subagent_type":"Explore","task_description":"Find sender initialization code"}

Everything else is explanation.\n28\t\n29\t---\n30\t\n31\t## 1. Objective\n32\t\n33\t> **A static website that accepts a file from the user and turns it into a visual\n34\t> transmission on screen, which a second device running the same page receives through\n35\t> its camera and reconstructs into the original file.**\n36\t>\n37\t> **It must handle large files — on the order of multiple gigabytes.**\n38\t\n39\t- **Static.** No backend. Files on a CDN, works offline, auditable once and trusted\n40\t  thereafter. There is nowhere to upload anything *to*.\n41\t- **Same page, both roles.** One deployment; the user picks sender or receiver.\n42\t- **Screen → camera is the only channel.** Strictly one-way, lossy, low-bandwidth.\n43\t- **Multi-gigabyte.** The requirement that most shapes the architecture (§3).\n44\t\n45\t### 1.1 The honest framing of \"multiple gigabytes\"\n46\t\n47\tMulti-GB support is an **architectural** requirement, not a performance promise. The\n48\tdesign must never *forbid* a large file, run out of memory, or blow up super-linearly.\n49\tBut the channel's physics are what they are:\n50\t\n51\t| File size | Stage 1 (30 KB/s) | Stage 2 (60 KB/s) | Stage 3 (106 KB/s) |\n52\t|---|---|---|---|\n53\t| 100 MB | 57 min | 28 min | 16 min |\n54\t| **1 GB** | **9.7 h** | **4.9 h** | **2.7 h** |\n55\t| **10 GB** | **4.0 days** | **2.0 days** | **27.5 h** |\n56\t| 100 GB | 40.5 days | 20.2 days | 11.4 days |\n57\t| 1 TB | 414 days | 207 days | 117 days |\n58\t\n59\t> All figures are **user-visible file bytes**, not wire bytes. See §13.2 — with\n60\t> compression on, the two differ by 3–10× on compressible input, and quoting the wrong\n61\t> one would overstate throughput.\n62\t\n63\t**Gigabytes are hours-to-days. Terabytes are months.** Three design consequences follow,\n64\tand they are as load-bearing as any coding decision:\n65\t\n66\t1. **Resume is not optional** (D22). Nobody holds a phone for 27 hours.\n67\t2. **Neither side may hold the file in memory** (D20).\n68\t3. **The app states the estimated time before the user commits** (D23). Letting someone\n69\t   start a 40-day transfer without saying so is a product failure, not an edge case.\n70\t\n71\t---\n72\t\n73\t## 2. Glossary\n74\t\n75\tSeveral of these words are overloaded in the surrounding literature, and two of them\n76\t(*block*, *frame*) mean different things in different research documents. Within this\n77\tplan they mean exactly this:\n78\t\n79\t| Term | Meaning here |\n80\t|---|---|\n81\t| **Fragment** | The atomic unit the fountain code operates over. Fixed length **L** for the whole session (D15). |\n82\t| **K** | Number of fragments in one block. Derived as `blockSize / L`; never transmitted (D7). |\n83\t| **Block** | A contiguous slice of the (possibly compressed) payload, cut into K fragments and fountain-coded independently. **Always means this** — never \"fountain block\" or \"QR block\". |\n84\t| **Packet** | One fountain-coded symbol: 13-byte header + L payload bytes. The unit a tile carries. |\n85\t| **Tile** | One QR symbol on screen. Carries exactly one packet. |\n86\t| **Frame** | One displayed image, containing a grid of tiles. **Never** a video frame — those are *camera frames*. |\n87\t| **Camera frame** | One image captured by the receiver's camera. |\n88\t| **Beacon** | A special frame carrying file-level metadata instead of payload (D17, §7.2). |\n89\t| **Profile** | A modulation configuration: QR version, module pixel size, tile count. Several coexist per frame (D16). |\n90\t| **Dwell** | How many packets the sender emits for one block before advancing (§8.1). |\n91\t| **Screen px** | A pixel on the *sender's display*. What the renderer controls. |\n92\t| **Camera px** | A pixel in the *receiver's captured frame*. What the decoder actually sees. |\n93\t| **px/module** | **Always CAMERA px per module unless explicitly written \"screen px/module\".** The 4 px/module decode cliff is a *camera*-pixel figure. Conflating the two put every S2/S3 optical run below the cliff — see `../notes/spike-results.md` §S3. |\n94\t| **Magnification** | `camera_px_per_module = screen_px_per_module × M`, where `M` = (capture width across the code region) / (code region width in screen px). A 1920-px-wide landscape code region filling a 1080-px-wide portrait capture gives **M = 0.5625**, so 4 screen px/module is only **2.25 camera px/module**. |\n95\t| **Erasure** | A packet that did not arrive or failed validation. Never a corrupted packet — those are discarded, not used. |\n96\t| **Stage** | A modulation generation: 1 = tiled mono QR, 2 = + RGB tripling, 3 = custom grid codec. |\n97\t| **Pass** | One complete traversal of every block by the sender. |\n98\t\n99\t---\n100\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":"call_ab7afd1283974e1c9e847367","session_id":"c99a1aaf-2bac-4a1c-9621-cc373f75e651","uuid":"c0d5e893-f4a9-4316-8d07-1689858965f7","timestamp":"2026-08-02T16:06:15.469Z","subagent_type":"Explore","task_description":"Find sender initialization code"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"id":"msg_20260803000715b3b17b7b434646e3","type":"message","role":"assistant","model":"glm-4.7","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"call_49dd165116154a4a99718a88","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/coding/screenferry/docs/notes/bf-4pc5-sender-compression-resume-detection.md","content":"# Sender-Side Compression/Resume Conflict Detection (bf-4pc5)\n\n**Bead:** `bf-4pc5`\n**Phase:** Phase 4 (Large-file machinery)\n**Related:** `bf-3k90` (Compression/Resume Solution Evaluation), `bf-2vke` (Compression/Resume/T4-Reap Interaction)\n\n## Executive Summary\n\nImplements **sender-side detection** for the architectural conflict between compression and resume. When both features are enabled together, this creates an invalid state that would silently corrupt receiver state. The detection happens during sender initialization, before any staging files are created or read.\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nFrom `bf-2vke` and `bf-17s0`:\n- **CompressionStream offers no determinism guarantee** across browser restarts\n- **Re-compression after staging reaping (E11) may produce different bytes**\n- **Different bytes → different block boundaries → different hashes**\n- **Receiver's persisted bitmap becomes silently invalid**\n\nThe receiver-side checks (`canResumeRecv()`, `createResumeToken()`) prevent resume when compression is enabled, but **sender-side validation was missing**. This meant a sender could be configured with both compression and resume enabled, leading to undefined behavior.\n\n## Solution: Fail-Fast Detection\n\nImplemented a validation module (`src/core/sender-validation.ts`) that:\n\n1. **Validates sender configuration** before initialization\n2. **Throws `CompressionResumeConflictError`** when both compression and resume are enabled\n3. **Provides non-throwing variants** for flexible use cases\n4. **Documents the architectural constraint** in error messages\n\n### Usage\n\n```typescript\nimport { validateSenderConfig, type SenderConfig } from './core/sender-validation.js';\n\n// During sender initialization\nconst config: SenderConfig = {\n  compressionEnabled: userSelectedCompression,\n  resumeEnabled: userSelectedResume,\n};\n\n// Fail-fast detection - throws if invalid\nvalidateSenderConfig(config);\n\n// If we reach here, config is valid - proceed with sender startup\n// - Create staging files (if compression enabled)\n// - Set beacon flags appropriately\n// - Start transmission\n```\n\n### Non-Throwing Variants\n\nFor scenarios where exception handling is undesirable:\n\n```typescript\nimport { isValidSenderConfig, getValidationError } from './core/sender-validation.js';\n\n// Check validity without throwing\nif (!isValidSenderConfig(config)) {\n  const error = getValidationError(config);\n  // Show user-friendly error in UI\n  console.error(error);\n  return;\n}\n```\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Validation Module\n\nLocated at `src/core/sender-validation.ts`:\n\n**Core Function:**\n- `validateSenderConfig(config: SenderConfig): void` - Throws on invalid config\n\n**Helper Functions:**\n- `isValidSenderConfig(config: SenderConfig): boolean` - Non-throwing check\n- `getValidationError(config: SenderConfig): string | null` - Error message\n\n**Error Type:**\n- `CompressionResumeConflictError` - When both features are enabled together, this creates an invalid state that would silently corrupt receiver state. The detection happens during sender initialization, before any staging files are created or read.\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nFrom `bf-2vke` and `bf-17s0`:\n- **CompressionStream offers no determinism guarantee** across browser restarts\n- **Re-compression after staging reaping (E11) may produce different bytes**\n- **Different bytes → different block boundaries → different hashes**\n- **Receiver's persisted bitmap becomes silently invalid**\n\nThe receiver-side checks (`canResumeRecv()`, `createResumeToken()`) prevent resume when compression is enabled, but **sender-side validation was missing**. This meant a sender could be configured with both compression and resume enabled, leading to undefined behavior.\n\n## Solution: Fail-Fast Detection\n\nImplemented a validation module (`src/core/sender-validation.ts`) that:\n\n1. **Validates sender configuration** before initialization\n2. **Throws `CompressionResumeConflictError`** when both compression and resume are enabled\n3. **Provides non-throwing variants** for flexible use cases\n4. **Documents the architectural constraint** in error messages\n\n### Usage\n\n```typescript\nimport { validateSenderConfig, type SenderConfig } from './core/sender-validation.js';\n\n// During sender initialization\nconst config: SenderConfig = {\n  compressionEnabled: userSelectedCompression,\n  resumeEnabled: userSelectedResume,\n};\n\n// Fail-fast detection - throws if invalid\nvalidateSenderConfig(config);\n\n// If we reach here, config is valid - proceed with sender startup\n// - Create staging files (if compression enabled)\n// - Set beacon flags appropriately\n// - Start transmission\n```\n\n### Non-Throwing Variants\n\nFor scenarios where exception handling is undesirable:\n\n```typescript\nimport { isValidSenderConfig, getValidationError } from './core/sender-validation.js';\n\n// Check validity without throwing\nif (!isValidSenderConfig(config)) {\n  const error = getValidationError(config);\n  // Show user-friendly error in UI\n  console.error(error);\n  return;\n}\n```\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Validation Module\n\nLocated at `src/core/sender-validation.ts`:\n\n**Core Function:**\n- `validateSenderConfig(config: SenderConfig): void` -
